title: Right Answer, Wrong Mechanism: Detecting Pernicious Divergence in Causal Interventions
abstract: arXiv:2609.39243v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Causal interventions such as activation patching and distributed alignment search (DAS) are the main tool for making mechanistic claims about neural networks. Recent work showed that these interventions routinely push representations off the model's natural distribution, and that such divergence is sometimes harmless and sometimes pernicious: it can recruit pathways the model never uses on natural inputs, so that an intervention produces the expected answer through the wrong mechanism. No method currently tells the two cases apart. We make this question testable by planting hidden pathways inside pretrained language models; the pathways are silent on every benchmark prompt by construction, so which interventions depend on them is known exactly. translated_title: 正确答案，错误机制：检测因果干预中的有害分歧
translated_abstract: 诸如激活修补和分布式对齐搜索（DAS）等因果干预是对神经网络做出机制性解释的主要工具。近期研究表明，这些干预通常会将表示推离模型的自然分布，而这种分歧有时无害，有时有害：它可能调用模型在自然输入上从不使用的路径，从而使干预通过错误的机制产生预期的答案。目前尚无方法能够区分这两种情况。我们通过在预训练语言模型中植入隐藏路径，使这一问题变得可检验；这些路径在构造上对所有基准提示都是沉默的，因此哪些干预依赖于它们是确切已知的。在GPT-2 small上的72种配置和100,800次干预中，我们有三项发现。(i) 先前工作中使用的干预位置处的最近邻和局部PCA距离，得分低于…（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文通过在预训练语言模型中植入隐藏路径来检测因果干预是否通过错误机制产生正确答案，并发现现有的基于距离的检测方法（如最近邻和局部PCA距离）不足以识别这种有害分歧。
en_tdlr: The paper plants hidden pathways in pretrained language models to make pernicious divergence in causal interventions testably detectable, finding that existing distance-based detection methods (nearest-neighbour and local-PCA distances) are insufficient to identify when interventions produce correct answers through wrong mechanisms.
